## Design note

The modern weapon. Lighter than the V10 by almost 200 kg and with far more torque, it is the hardest-accelerating rear-drive car in the city — and rear drive is the catch: on its factory track tyres it lights them up in third on a damp road. The active wing glues the rear down at speed, so it is calm and stable flat-out on the highway and nervous at 60 km/h on a roundabout. Hydraulic-feeling steering, quick rack, no slack.

## How this car breaks

Carbon-fibre tub with aluminium crash structures bolted front and rear. The tub itself is close to indestructible at street speeds, but everything bolted to it is sacrificial: the front crash box and radiators fold early, the rear subframe carries the V8, turbos and gearbox, so a rear hit kills drive. Carbon panels crack and shed rather than dent; the dihedral doors pop open in side hits.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

## Engine

4.0 L DOHC 32-valve flat-plane-crank V8, twin twin-scroll turbos, dry sump, intercooled, plateau 3500-5000 rpm. Class-typical 2020s 4.0 TT V8 supercar (~128 kW/L, ~513 kW at 7000 rpm, 800 N·m plateau) per manufacturer spec-class data and owner dyno sheets; the flat-plane crank revs freely, so the torque falls off late and steeply past 7000.

## Drivetrain

7-speed dual-clutch transaxle, clutch-type rear LSD standing in for the brake-based torque vectoring. Layout **RWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 50 N·m, power ramp 0.40, coast ramp 0.25. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 1120 N·m. Shift time 0.18 s.

| 7 | 0.76 | 2.52 | 402 |

Final drive 3.31, reverse 3.10. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.335 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.32 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 293 kg | 2.00 Hz | 46200 N/m | 2350 N·s/m | 3520 N·s/m | 0.11 m |
| Rear | 408 kg | 2.20 Hz | 77900 N/m | 3610 N·s/m | 5420 N·s/m | 0.12 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.4°/g with 52% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.297 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 177330 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 64413 F / 102190 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **10000 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.3°/g, front share 47%. Bump stops 200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.4° F / -1.8° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 6.5°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 390 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 36 mm + 34 mm → A = 30.6 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 170 mm, pad μ = 0.46: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.46·100 bar·30.6 cm²·0.170 m = **4786 N·m**
- Rear: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 36 mm + 32 mm → A = 18.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.44: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.44·100 bar·18.2 cm²·0.165 m = **2646 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 4786 / 2646 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.36), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.56 → **2690 / 1490 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1320 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.04×), rear needs 1052 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.42×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 2145 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2690 N·m front / 1490 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 2130 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 13.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 12.0 m → outer-front path radius 5.88 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.40 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.545 rad (31.2°)** (outer 27.0°, inner 36.8° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 1.8 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/halberd_40.json`)

276 nodes, 1772 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id halberd_40 --profile coupe --width 1.93 --length 4.54 --height 1.2 --wheelbase 2.67 --mass 297.6 --car-mass 1488.2 --clearance 0.11 --front-overhang 0.98 --strength 1.0` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2020s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Carbon-fibre monocoque tub (stiffer than an HSS cell): 384 passenger-cell beams (cabin, sills, pillars, roof rails, cross-members) × 1.25 section.
- Aluminium body: 610 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.87…-1.52 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 166 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
